system.name: WM-ABench
system.one_liner: A two-stage (perception, prediction) atomic benchmark testing whether vision-language models hold internal world models, over 23 dimensions in 6 simulators.

content.variant_note: framework loop and dimension taxonomy at left, two radial bar charts of model-vs-human scores at centre-right, four tinted question cards at the corners tied to the charts by dashed leaders
content.argues: A world model splits into perception and prediction stages made of atomic abilities, and seven current VLMs fall well short of humans on most of them.
content.subject: an agent-environment loop with its perception and prediction dimensions, per-dimension scores of seven VLMs against humans, and four sample benchmark items with model answers

lessons.what_to_learn: Reuse the dimension names of the framework as the sector labels of the result charts and tie tinted example cards to the charts with dashed leaders, so framework, evidence and instances read as one composite. A translucent human band behind model bars shows the gap at a glance.
lessons.suits: benchmark papers that define a capability taxonomy, report per-dimension scores of several models against humans, and want real items with model answers in the same figure.

evidence: We decompose the process into two stages: (1) perception stage, which involves visual, spatial, temporal, quantitative, and motion perceptions
Large-scale evaluation reveals VLMs' limitations as WMs.
all models perform at near-random accuracy when distinguishing motion trajectories

summary: WM-ABench is a benchmark that asks whether vision-language models hold internal world models. The paper splits a world model into a perception stage (visual, spatial, temporal, quantity, motion) and a prediction stage (mechanistic simulation, transitive and compositional inference), tested through 23 dimensions over 6 simulators. Figure 1 packs the framework, the results and sample items into one dashboard. At left, an agent loop from environment through sensory signals, perception, prediction and action carries yellow and pink callouts that list the dimensions with small icons. At centre and right, two radial bar charts show seven VLMs' accuracy per dimension against translucent human bands. Four corner cards, tinted to match the stage they test, show simulator renders with each model's answer, wrong ones highlighted, tied to the charts by dashed leaders.
summary_zh: WM-ABench 评测视觉语言模型是否具备内部世界模型。图一把框架、结果和样例拼成一张总览：左侧是环境、感知、预测、动作的循环及各维度图标，右侧两张径向柱状图对比7个模型与人类，四角的题目卡片用虚线连到对应图表。
notes: Prior labels listed contribution-mosaic first; scope-overview (benchmark-dashboard) is primary here because the taxonomy, per-dimension statistics and examples form one linked composite. The loop at left is the paper's conceptual framework, not an evaluated method. Which sector each dashed leader points to is not clear from the figure. Panel verdicts on the two charts mark the gap to humans the figure argues for.
